title: Routing justification stream with deduped context summaries
creator: Asha Kapoor
description:
Problem: Our existing route-level telemetry emits full per-hop decision payloads which are large and often duplicate identical routing context (customer routing policy, pinned model variant, region preference, fallback chain). This inflates ingestion cost, makes downstream query and anomaly detection slow, and increases signal noise when tracing multi-hop fallbacks across regions.

Goal: Implement a streaming "routing justification" pipeline that emits small, deduplicated context summaries and delta events per request hop, plus a compact canonical context store for infrequent full materializations. The stream should preserve provenance (trace_id, request_id, hop_index), provide a stable dedupe key for identical contexts, and expose per-hop condensed metrics (decision_latency_ms, model_variant_cost_units, fallback_reason) for SLO and RCA.

Proposal:
1) Define a canonical context schema (json-ld style flat keys) limited to ~6-10 fields that affect routing: region_preference, tier_allowed, model_family, quantization_profile, customer_override, sticky_route_id. Only canonical contexts are written to the context-store.
2) For each routing hop emit a light-weight event: {trace_id, request_id, hop_index, context_key, delta_flags, decision_code, decision_latency_ms, model_variant_cost_units, sampling_rate}. Events reference context_key instead of embedding full context.
3) Build a compact context-store service (TTL-based, cross-region replication optional) that holds contexts keyed by a stable hash (context_key). Context-store supports GetByKey and CreateIfMissing with optimistic dedupe.
4) Streaming infra: route events into the existing telemetry bus (kafka/topic 'routing-justifications') with partitioning by trace_id to preserve ordering for a request. Consumers: Console observability UI, SLO alerting, RCA job, and a nightly compaction job producing per-route aggregates.
5) Sampling and retention: full contexts are sampled at 0.5% by default (configurable per-customer/mode). Deduped contexts are retained for 30 days by default; events retained according to existing telemetry retention (30 days hot, archive thereafter).

Trade-offs & considerations:
- Pros: reduces average event size by >6x, lowers ingestion cost, faster joins in analytics, clearer per-hop metrics for SLOs.
- Cons: adds a context-store dependency and eventual consistency window where consumers may query a key that is not yet materialized. Mitigation: emit a transient full_context field in the first hop for the request if CreateIfMissing fails, and backfill asynchronously.
- Privacy: context fields exclude PII and customer-sensitive prompt tokens. KMS encryption at rest for context-store required for Private deployments.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 1 (canary): Emit events referencing context_key and write to a shadow topic for 1% traffic. Also log full_context in shadow events to validate dedupe and correctness.
- Phase 2 (validation): Run backfill job to ensure context-store hit rate >99% for live requests. Run analytics to compare SLO signal with legacy stream.
- Phase 3 (switch): Switch consumers to new topic and retire legacy per-hop full payload events.

Acceptance criteria (see field "acceptance_criteria" below) and monitoring dashboards to be published in Console under "Routing / Justification".
acceptance_criteria: New lightweight hop events published to routing-justifications topic and contain context_key reference
Context-store can resolve 99% of context_key lookups for live traffic during canary
End-to-end query (trace_id -> all hops with expanded contexts) completes within SLA (5s) for 95th percentile in the console
Average per-event payload size reduced by >=6x vs legacy per-hop full payloads
Nightly compaction job produces per-route cost and latency aggregates compatible with existing SLOs
Security review completed and KMS encryption enabled for context-store in Private deployments
